title_missing.explanation: Search engines use the <title> as the headline of the result. Without one they invent it.

title_too_short.explanation: Titles under 30 characters waste the space searchers use to decide to click.

title_too_long.explanation: Titles over 60 characters are truncated in results, hiding the end.

title_duplicate.explanation: Pages sharing a title compete with each other and look like duplicates to crawlers.

meta_description_missing.explanation: Without a meta description, search engines pick an arbitrary snippet from the page.

meta_description_too_short.explanation: Descriptions under 70 characters rarely say enough to earn the click.

meta_description_too_long.explanation: Descriptions over 160 characters are cut off in results.

meta_description_duplicate.explanation: A description reused across pages cannot describe any of them well.

h1_missing.explanation: The <h1> tells crawlers and screen readers what the page is about.

h1_multiple.explanation: Several <h1> elements dilute the page's main topic.

thin_content.explanation: Pages with under 300 words of visible text rarely rank; they look empty to crawlers.

canonical_missing.explanation: A self-referencing canonical protects the page from being treated as a duplicate of parameterised or mirrored copies.

canonical_conflict.explanation: A canonical pointing at another page tells search engines to index that page instead.

canonical_off_domain.explanation: A canonical on another domain hands this page's ranking to that domain.

noindex.explanation: A noindex robots meta removes the page from search results entirely.

nofollow.explanation: A nofollow robots meta stops crawlers following any link on the page.

x_robots_tag.explanation: An X-Robots-Tag header blocks indexing invisibly; it never shows up in the HTML.

images_missing_alt.explanation: Images without an alt attribute are invisible to image search and screen readers. An empty alt="" is fine for decorative images and is not flagged.

broken_links.explanation: Internal links to 4xx/5xx pages waste crawl budget and send visitors to error pages.

orphan_page.explanation: A page in the sitemap that no other page links to gets little crawl attention and no internal ranking signal.

redirect_chain.explanation: Each extra redirect hop adds latency and leaks link equity; one hop is normal, more is not.

page_too_heavy.explanation: HTML over 2 MB is slow on mobile and may be truncated by crawlers.

slow_response.explanation: Server responses over 2000 ms hurt both rankings and crawl rate.

lang_missing.explanation: <html lang> tells search engines and screen readers which language the page is in.

og_missing.explanation: Open Graph title and description control how the page looks when shared on social media.
